description: Public catalog of deterministic rules shipped with AIsec. Evidence levels describe the default static signal, while applicability and review fields document bounded coverage rather than exploitability or certification.

languages: Selected text source and configuration files
applicabilityProfiles.versionStatement: No package-version gate is applied; only the documented credential or source-code syntax is recognized.
No runtime or framework semver is inferred; the bounded TypeScript parser and recognized local syntax determine coverage.
Applies to recognized app/api/**/route source layout and exported HTTP handlers without checking the installed Next.js version.
GitHub Actions is not package-versioned; coverage is limited to recognized workflow run-step expression syntax.
No FastAPI dependency range is asserted; only statically resolved decorators, routers, dependencies and middleware patterns are covered.
No Express dependency range is asserted; only bounded static router, middleware, controller and local-call patterns are covered.
No NestJS dependency range is asserted; only bounded official decorators, module graphs, bootstrap calls, RouterModule trees and local-call patterns are covered.
No Python runtime version is inferred; coverage depends on the bounded recognized source syntax and local call graph.
No JWT library version is inferred; only recognized production-named configuration keys and literal values are evaluated.
Coverage correlates recognized Compose port publication with statically visible FastAPI routes; neither dependency nor Compose schema semver is used as a gate.
No Supabase or PostgreSQL version is inferred; only scanned migration statements and recognized RLS policy syntax are evaluated.
Rules-version declarations are not used as a gate; coverage is limited to recognized unconditional allow syntax in scanned rule files.
Android API level is not inferred; the rule reports recognized effective-looking manifest attributes and requires build-variant review.
iOS deployment target is not inferred; coverage is limited to recognized App Transport Security keys in scanned property lists.
Framework and platform versions are not inferred; only recognized JavaScript/bridge enablement syntax is reported.
Platform and framework versions are not inferred; only recognized production-looking cleartext URL literals are reported.
No React Native or AsyncStorage version is inferred; coverage is limited to recognized sensitive-key setItem calls.
No Flutter or package version is inferred; coverage is limited to recognized SharedPreferences, WebView and TLS callback syntax.
Platform versions are not inferred; only bounded selected resources and printable strings from validated archives are inspected.
The bundled rule is integration-tested with the single verified Opengrep version declared by AIsec.

rules.summary: Stripe live secret key in source
falsePositiveModes: A credential-shaped value may be synthetic, revoked or isolated to a fixture.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm provenance without sending the key, revoke any real credential, and inspect source history and built client assets.

rules.summary: OpenAI API key in source
falsePositiveModes: A credential-shaped value may be synthetic, revoked or isolated to a fixture.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm provenance without sending the key, revoke any real credential, and inspect source history and distributed bundles.

rules.summary: AWS access key in source
falsePositiveModes: The identifier may be synthetic, revoked or a non-authentic documentation example.
rules.reviewGuidance: Verify through account inventory rather than authentication attempts, rotate if real, and check paired secrets and Git history.

rules.summary: GitHub token in source
falsePositiveModes: The token-shaped value may be synthetic, revoked or fixture-only.
rules.reviewGuidance: Use repository/account audit records to establish validity, revoke any real token, and inspect workflow and history exposure.

rules.summary: Private key material committed to the project
falsePositiveModes: The block may be an intentionally invalid fixture or documentation placeholder.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm whether usable private material is present, replace the key pair if real, and remove it from repository and release history.

rules.summary: Privileged value exposed through a client-public environment variable
falsePositiveModes: A variable name may imply privilege while the actual value is intentionally public and least-privileged.
rules.reviewGuidance: Inspect the provider-side privileges and final client bundle; move any privileged capability behind an authenticated server operation.

rules.summary: Client code references a public-prefixed privileged variable
falsePositiveModes: The referenced value may be intentionally public despite a privileged-looking variable name.
rules.reviewGuidance: Trace the build-time value and provider permissions, then inspect compiled assets to confirm the effective exposure.

rules.summary: Request data reaches a database query without a visible parameter boundary
falsePositiveModes: Validation or parameterization may occur in an unsupported wrapper outside the bounded local flow.
rules.reviewGuidance: Trace the complete source-to-sink path and confirm values use bound parameters while identifiers use strict allowlists.

rules.summary: Request data reaches code or command execution
falsePositiveModes: The value may be reduced to a fixed allowlisted token by an unsupported helper before execution.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm whether any attacker-controlled bytes reach a shell, executable selection, eval or code constructor; prefer fixed argument vectors.

rules.summary: Request-controlled URL reaches a server-side network client
falsePositiveModes: A supported public-host allowlist may be enforced in an external wrapper not visible to the local flow.
rules.reviewGuidance: Verify scheme, host, port, DNS/IP range and every redirect target are server-controlled and reject private or metadata addresses.

rules.summary: Model output reaches a privileged execution sink
falsePositiveModes: A typed allowlist or human confirmation boundary may exist in an unsupported helper between model output and the sink.
rules.reviewGuidance: Require a typed tool schema, fixed operations, bounded arguments, least privilege and confirmation for consequential actions.

rules.summary: Untrusted data is assigned to an HTML execution sink
falsePositiveModes: A sanitizer may be applied through an unsupported alias or wrapper before assignment.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm the value is rendered as text or passed through a maintained context-appropriate sanitizer with a strict allowlist.

rules.summary: Untrusted data reaches dangerouslySetInnerHTML
falsePositiveModes: The raw HTML may be sanitized in an unsupported wrapper or come from an administrator-only trusted source.
rules.reviewGuidance: Avoid raw HTML where possible; otherwise verify provenance and strict sanitization immediately before the __html value is created.

rules.summary: Sensitive Next.js API route has no visible authentication guard
falsePositiveModes: Middleware, a gateway or a framework extension outside the route file may enforce authentication.
rules.reviewGuidance: Verify the deployed route with an unauthenticated request and locate the server-enforced identity and authorization boundary.

rules.summary: Untrusted GitHub event data is interpolated into a shell step
falsePositiveModes: The event value may be structurally constrained or the matched step may be unreachable for untrusted events.
rules.reviewGuidance: Inspect event triggers, permissions and shell expansion; pass event text through an environment variable as quoted data instead of script text.

rules.summary: Potential credential or session data written to logs
falsePositiveModes: A sensitive-looking variable may already contain a fixed placeholder, hash or redacted representation.
rules.reviewGuidance: Inspect the runtime value and logger processors, then verify production logs cannot contain credentials, cookies or bearer tokens.

rules.summary: FastAPI sensitive route bypasses authentication through a global whitelist
falsePositiveModes: The route may be intentionally public or protected by an upstream control not visible in the project.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm the whitelist match and deployed middleware order, then test the exact route without credentials and with a low-privilege identity.

rules.summary: FastAPI sensitive route has no visible authentication guard
falsePositiveModes: An upstream gateway, dynamic dependency or unsupported middleware may enforce authentication.
rules.reviewGuidance: Locate the deployed identity boundary and verify an unauthenticated request receives 401 or 403.

rules.summary: FastAPI object operation has no visible ownership or role check
falsePositiveModes: Ownership may be enforced by an unsupported ORM scope, policy engine, dependency or database view.
rules.reviewGuidance: Trace the object query to a server-controlled subject, tenant or privileged role and verify with two low-privilege accounts.

rules.summary: Express sensitive route has no visible authentication guard
falsePositiveModes: An upstream gateway, package middleware, dynamic mount or unsupported wrapper may enforce authentication.
rules.reviewGuidance: Locate the effective deployed middleware chain and verify an unauthenticated request receives 401 or 403.

rules.summary: Express object operation has no visible ownership or role check
falsePositiveModes: Ownership may be enforced in an unsupported ORM scope, policy engine, package base class or complex helper.
rules.reviewGuidance: Trace the object query to the authenticated subject or tenant and verify cross-account identifiers receive 403 or 404.

rules.summary: Express privileged operation has no visible role or permission check
falsePositiveModes: The route name may look privileged while the operation is harmless, or authorization may live in an unsupported policy layer.
rules.reviewGuidance: Identify the required permission and verify an authenticated low-privilege account is denied before business logic executes.

rules.summary: NestJS sensitive route has no visible authentication guard
falsePositiveModes: A gateway, mixin/package guard, dynamic module or unsupported bootstrap wrapper may enforce authentication.
rules.reviewGuidance: Locate the effective global/controller/route guard and verify the deployed route rejects unauthenticated callers.

rules.summary: NestJS object operation has no visible ownership or role check
falsePositiveModes: Ownership may be enforced in an unsupported provider, ORM scope, policy engine, mixin or package base class.
rules.reviewGuidance: Trace the object query through providers to a subject/tenant constraint and verify cross-account access with two low-privilege accounts.

rules.summary: NestJS privileged operation has no visible role or permission check
falsePositiveModes: The composed path may look administrative while the operation is harmless, or an unsupported policy layer may authorize it.
rules.reviewGuidance: Identify the effective module/controller/route policy and verify a low-privilege identity is denied before the privileged action.

rules.summary: Request-derived URL reaches a Python network client
falsePositiveModes: A strict host/IP allowlist may exist in an unsupported helper outside the bounded local flow.
rules.reviewGuidance: Review scheme, host, port, DNS resolution and redirects, and ensure private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses are rejected.

rules.summary: Request-derived path reaches or feeds a server file operation
falsePositiveModes: Canonicalization under a fixed root may occur in an unsupported helper or storage abstraction.
rules.reviewGuidance: Require opaque server identifiers, canonicalize under a fixed root, reject absolute/traversal paths and verify the final path remains inside the root.

rules.summary: Request-derived data is interpolated into Python SQL
falsePositiveModes: Parameterization or identifier allowlisting may occur in an unsupported query wrapper.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm values are bound parameters and any dynamic identifiers come from a strict server-side allowlist.

rules.summary: Client-controlled model URL can receive a server-side API key
falsePositiveModes: The destination may be normalized to a server allowlist or the credential may be destination-bound in an unsupported wrapper.
rules.reviewGuidance: Ensure callers cannot choose credential destinations; bind each server secret to a fixed allowlisted provider origin.

rules.summary: FastAPI allows credentialed CORS from a wildcard origin
falsePositiveModes: Middleware may normalize the combination into a non-wildcard response, or no browser credential flow may exist.
rules.reviewGuidance: Inspect actual preflight/response headers and declare exact trusted origins, methods and headers for browser credential flows.

rules.summary: FastAPI returns raw internal exception text to clients
falsePositiveModes: The caught exception type or string conversion may produce only a fixed client-safe message.
rules.reviewGuidance: Exercise representative failures and confirm clients receive a fixed message/correlation ID while details stay only in protected server logs.

rules.summary: JWT signing secret is committed in a production configuration
falsePositiveModes: A production-named file may be a synthetic fixture or the value may be an intentionally invalid placeholder.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm provenance without signing tokens, rotate any real key, remove it from history and load replacements from a secret manager.

rules.summary: JWT access token lifetime exceeds one day
falsePositiveModes: The literal may describe a refresh/non-bearer token or compensating revocation may sharply limit effective lifetime.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm token type and deployed value; prefer short-lived access tokens with rotation, audience/issuer checks and revocation controls.

rules.summary: Production Compose publishes an API service with unguarded FastAPI routes
falsePositiveModes: A host firewall, authenticated reverse proxy or private deployment network may prevent direct reachability.
rules.reviewGuidance: Inspect the effective deployment and bind internal services to private networks/loopback while also enforcing service identity in the app.

rules.summary: Supabase application table is created without enabling RLS
falsePositiveModes: RLS may be enabled by an unscanned migration, provisioning step or generated schema outside the repository.
rules.reviewGuidance: Inspect the deployed database catalog and migration order, then require explicit least-privilege policies for every client-accessible operation.

rules.summary: Supabase RLS policy unconditionally allows access
falsePositiveModes: The policy may target an intentionally public table, a narrow role or only one deliberately public operation.
rules.reviewGuidance: Review target roles and commands in the deployed policy and bind private rows to auth.uid(), tenant membership or another trusted claim.

rules.summary: Firebase security rule grants unconditional access
falsePositiveModes: The matched path may intentionally contain public data or the scanned rule file may not be the deployed ruleset.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm the deployed rules and data sensitivity, then require request.auth plus ownership/tenant checks for non-public operations.

rules.summary: Android application permits cleartext network traffic
falsePositiveModes: The manifest may belong only to a debug flavor or be overridden during the release manifest merge.
rules.reviewGuidance: Inspect the merged release manifest and Network Security Configuration, and restrict any development exception to non-release builds.

rules.summary: Android application data backup is enabled
falsePositiveModes: Release data-extraction rules may exclude all sensitive data or the manifest may be debug-only.
rules.reviewGuidance: Inspect the merged release manifest and backup/data-extraction rules, then verify credentials and private records are excluded.

rules.summary: iOS App Transport Security is globally disabled
falsePositiveModes: The property list may be test-only, unused by the release target or replaced during build.
rules.reviewGuidance: Inspect the signed release app Info.plist and remove the global exception, retaining only justified narrow HTTPS-compatible exceptions.

rules.summary: Mobile WebView enables an elevated JavaScript capability
falsePositiveModes: The WebView may load only bundled trusted content, block navigation and expose no sensitive native methods.
rules.reviewGuidance: Review every load/navigation source, origin allowlist, bridge method and message schema; disable JavaScript/bridges when not required.

rules.summary: Mobile source references a cleartext HTTP endpoint
falsePositiveModes: The URL may be unreachable test data, documentation, a non-release branch or a harmless local-network development endpoint.
rules.reviewGuidance: Trace the literal into the release build and runtime traffic; production endpoints must use HTTPS with normal certificate validation.

rules.summary: Sensitive value stored in React Native AsyncStorage
falsePositiveModes: The sensitive-looking key may store a non-secret marker, short-lived public identifier or already protected envelope.
rules.reviewGuidance: Inspect the runtime value and use Keychain/Keystore-backed storage for credentials, keeping tokens short-lived and revocable.

rules.summary: Sensitive value stored in Flutter SharedPreferences
falsePositiveModes: The sensitive-looking key may contain only a non-secret marker or already protected value.
rules.reviewGuidance: Inspect the stored value and use platform secure storage for credentials, with short lifetimes and server-side revocation.

rules.summary: Flutter WebView enables unrestricted JavaScript
falsePositiveModes: The WebView may be restricted to bundled trusted content with external navigation and bridges disabled.
rules.reviewGuidance: Review all origins, navigation callbacks and channels; disable JavaScript when possible and strictly validate every bridge message.

rules.summary: Flutter networking accepts invalid TLS certificates
falsePositiveModes: The callback may be confined to a compile-time debug branch that is absent from the release artifact.
rules.reviewGuidance: Inspect the release build path and remove unconditional acceptance; use a development-only trust store for local certificates.

rules.summary: Credential embedded in a distributed mobile artifact
falsePositiveModes: A recoverable credential-shaped string may be synthetic, revoked or unused decoy data.
rules.reviewGuidance: Establish provenance without authenticating, revoke any real credential and move privileged operations behind a server boundary.

rules.summary: Cleartext endpoint embedded in a mobile artifact
falsePositiveModes: The string may be unused, test-only, documentation or dead code retained in the artifact.
rules.reviewGuidance: Confirm runtime reachability and release traffic, then replace production cleartext endpoints and remove fallback strings before rebuilding.

rules.summary: Packaged iOS app disables App Transport Security
falsePositiveModes: A matching property-list fragment may be an unused bundled resource rather than the effective application Info.plist.
rules.reviewGuidance: Inspect the signed app's effective Info.plist and remove global ATS disablement, retaining only narrow documented exceptions.

rules.summary: JavaScript or TypeScript uses eval or the Function constructor
falsePositiveModes: The executed text may be a fixed trusted constant, generated code or an intentionally isolated sandbox input.
rules.reviewGuidance: Determine input provenance and execution privileges; remove dynamic evaluation or replace it with a fixed parser/operation allowlist.

rules.summary: Python deserializes data with pickle.load or pickle.loads
falsePositiveModes: The serialized bytes may come only from a trusted local build artifact with an authenticated integrity boundary.
rules.reviewGuidance: Trace byte provenance and integrity; prefer a non-executable format and never unpickle data controlled by users or remote systems.

rules.summary: MD5 or SHA-1 is used through a recognized hash API
falsePositiveModes: The hash may be used only as a non-security checksum, cache key or compatibility identifier.
rules.reviewGuidance: Identify the security property: use a modern password KDF for passwords and SHA-256 or stronger for signatures/integrity.
